title: Cross-mesh soakbench and p95 drift sentinel for TP/PP distributed inference
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible soak and microburst benchmark that exercises tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) meshes across heterogeneous clusters and surfaces tokens/sec, p95 latency, and automated regression alerts. This ticket covers harness design, measurement instrumentation, alerting heuristics, and initial runbook for investigating p95 drift.

Scope: multi-node runs (2-8 nodes), mix of A100/H100 hardware, several TPxPP topologies (e.g., 1x4, 2x2, 4x1), sequence lengths {128,512,2048}, KV-cache cold vs warm profiles, and both sustained and burst load patterns. The harness should emit per-route and per-model aggregates: tokens/sec (q50/q90/q99), latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, and concurrency distribution. Also include drift detection and auto-classification of regression signals (transient vs sustained).

Acceptance criteria: harness can reproduce baseline numbers within 5% for tokens/sec on reference model; p95 regression detector triggers with <10% false-positive rate on synthetic noise; runs are automatable in CI with configurable node topology and load profile; results archive to S3 and a summary is published to the Console dashboard ingest endpoint.

Design notes: we will reuse the existing job orchestration framework (kube-job-runner) but introduce a new runner shim (sentrybench-runner) to coordinate cross-node KV prefill, staggered client ramps, and controlled microbursts. Measurement will be taken at the client-side (load generators) and server-side traces (tracing hooks) to correlate tokens emitted vs kernel stalls. For regression detection we will implement an EWMA-based detector on p95 with windowed baseline and outlier suppression, and a secondary quantile-regression check for multi-modal latency distributions.

Risks and trade-offs: accurate p95 needs stable warmup and consistent KV cache state; aggressive caching in production can hide regression modes so tests include both cold and warmed runs. Heterogeneous hardware introduces variance — to control for that we will pin runs to predefined node labels and include normalization heuristics. Realistic traffic requires variable prompt length and multi-stream vs single-stream mixes; initial iteration will focus on single-stream and batched inference modes, followed by multi-stream variants in a follow-up ticket.

Artifacts and links: Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Cross-mesh+Soak+Plan ; design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/throughput-sentinel ; initial harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-sentinel ; PR for runner shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-sentinel/pull/246 ; dashboard ingestion spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/911.

Next steps: finalize detector thresholds with historical data, land runner shim PR, run three full soak passes (cold/warm/mixed) in staging, and submit summary to the SLO owners for review.
